entries.title: Trump waives several Russia sanctions as row with Zelensky intensifies
entries.snippet: The US president temporarily ends many restrictions on Moscow recently passed by Congress over "national security" concerns.

entries.title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms
entries.snippet: The Amazon rainforest is a crucial buffer against climate change - but deforestation had expanded under former president Jair Bolsonaro.

entries.title: Rare pink diamond goes on display in France 100 years after amateur heist

entries.title: Pope's health should not be taken 'for granted', says top Vatican diplomat
entries.snippet: Archbishop Paul Gallagher tells the BBC there was no sign of the Pope's ill health prior to his operation this week.

entries.title: No Kings turns its focus to voting this weekend. Here's what we know
entries.snippet: The coalition behind nationwide anti-Trump protests is shifting its strategies this weekend to focus on voter turnout. Organizers say Saturday's events are a nonpartisan effort to get people to the polls.

entries.title: Sidewalk sleepers: They have nowhere else to stay while a loved one is in the hospital
entries.snippet: Patients travel miles to be treated at public hospitals in Delhi. Those in need get financial aid for their care. But for overnight accommodations, families are often on their own — and on the street.

entries.title: Trump promised a swing district blitz. He's going to a lot of very red states
entries.snippet: President Trump's midterm travel blitz ahead of Election Day includes several red states he won easily 2 years ago, showing the electoral landscape is more challenging for Republicans.

entries.title: Weddings are expensive. How about a grocery store cake?
entries.snippet: About a third of couples are willing to save money on cake and dessert, according to the wedding-planning site Zola.

entries.title: Coastal homes burn as hot winds fuel California fires
entries.snippet: High winds are fueling a fast-moving fire that has burned homes in Southern California. Flames engulfed expensive coastal properties and prompted thousands to evacuate.

entries.title: Katie Zacharia is out as press secretary, White House says
entries.snippet: Katie Zacharia is "transitioning out" of her role as press secretary, according to a White House official not authorized to speak on the record, marking a stunning turn of events for the spokeswoman.

entries.snippet: Katie Zacharia's first official day was on Monday.

entries.title: Fundraising to protect key natural sites falls short ahead of UN biodiversity summit
entries.snippet: Efforts to raise hundreds of billions of dollars to preserve the world's oceans, forests, rivers, lakes and other parts of the natural world have fallen short ahead of a key U.N. summit on biodiversity.

entries.title: Israeli settlers attack Palestinians during West Bank olive harvest and beat U.S. photojournalist
entries.snippet: Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian villages across the occupied West Bank on Friday, setting fire to cars and trees and beating residents and a Washington Post photographer, in the latest violence to disrupt the territory's annual olive harvest this month.

entries.title: DOJ says California officials who process ballots from suspected noncitizens risk prosecution

entries.title: A rare family of barn owls moved into Manhattan's Upper West Side, captivating New Yorkers
entries.snippet: This is the first documented instance of barn owls nesting in Manhattan in modern history, according to one expert, and the owls have attracted nightly crowds of people in the street eager to get a glimpse of the elusive birds.

entries.snippet: Ahead of the midterms, President Trump is on the campaign trail looking to rally his base in battleground races. His controversial comments at those rallies have drawn attention. White House correspondent Liz Landers has a fact check on some of Trump's claims.

entries.title: Exhibition explores connection between Black women and the works of Shakespeare
entries.snippet: The Folger Shakespeare Library's newest exhibition maps an unlikely historical connection between Black women and the works of William Shakespeare. Nearly 100 objects document the stories of renowned scholars, popular actors and little-known historic figures. Geoff Bennett spoke

entries.title: China says it will curb tech exports, including AI, citing national security risks
entries.snippet: The proposal came as China and the U.S. made progress in dialogues over AI safety and governance and on the setting up of a notification mechanism between the two superpowers for AI incidents that could threaten national security.

entries.title: Arab-led parties could decide the Israeli election, if anyone would partner with them
entries.snippet: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his chief rivals have said they won't form a coalition with any Arab-led party after the Oct. 27 election – even if that means months of gridlock and another round of voting.

entries.title: Democrats say Trump increased investments in drugmakers that were given Medicare exemptions
entries.snippet: The report from congressional Democrats found that Trump's pharmaceutical stock holdings grew from a maximum reported value of $1.7 million in 2024 to as much as $56.2 million at the end of 2025.

entries.title: Community leaders say foiled Hindu temple attack was result of surge in online hate
entries.snippet: A thwarted mass shooting targeting a large Hindu temple in suburban Chicago was fueled by years of hateful rhetoric on social media against Hindus and Indians, community leaders say.

entries.title: LA fire survivors set to lose case managers as California and FEMA's standoff drags on
entries.snippet: The program's early termination is the latest setback for Los Angeles communities in the middle of recovery and awaiting billions of additional federal dollars.

entries.title: Man who stopped the Oregon elementary school shooter has 2 daughters at the school, his mom says
entries.snippet: Kenda Freeman said her son, Kaylub Giamanco, intervened in Thursday's attack at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend and shot the teenage shooter.

entries.title: More roller coasters shut down as authorities investigate fatal fall at Georgia amusement park
entries.snippet: Sea World Orlando in Florida and La Ronde theme park in Montreal, Canada, confirmed they had temporarily closed rides, bringing the total number of roller coasters halted to 11.

entries.title: Prime Minister Mark Carney says U.S. is trying to break Canada as Alberta votes on separation path
entries.snippet: "This referendum comes at the worst possible time," Carney told a large pro-Canada rally in Calgary. "The world has become more dangerous and divided. Some outside our borders are working to break us so they can own us."

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Germany news: Merz faces conservative youth wing in Bonn
entries.snippet: Friedrich Merz, who has struggled for support within his party, on Saturday meets with the CDU/CSU's 90,000-strong Young Union. In Schleswig-Holstein, 3,000 people are expected at an AfD youth rally. DW has more.

entries.title: Mexico sentences killers of US, Australian surfers to 158 years each in prison
entries.snippet: Three Mexican men were found guilty last week of murdering foreign surfers in 2024. The case had drawn global condemnation, particularly in Australia, where two of the victims were from.

entries.title: France braces for nationwide protests
entries.snippet: Students, trade unionists and Yellow Vest activists are taking to French streets to protest high prices and inequality. Authorities say they fear the rallies could turn violent.

entries.title: India news: 'Cockroach' party founder Abhijeet Dipke under preventive arrest
entries.snippet: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke is due to appear before a Special Executive Magistrate later in the day. Dipke was detained ahead of a demonstration in New Delhi on Friday. DW has more.

entries.title: US: California wildfires destroy homes, leave thousands without power
entries.snippet: Multiple mansions have been engulfed in the fires raging in California while firefighters continue to douse the blaze. Thousands of people have been evacuated and many others are without power.

entries.title: Oregon school shooting: Police praise 'heroism' of those who intervened to stop more killing
entries.snippet: US police have praised the actions of three people who cut short a deadly shooting at a school in the state of Oregon. Three children and a teacher were killed in the attack, carried out by a former pupil at the school.

entries.title: Trump puts new Russia sanctions on hold
entries.snippet: The US president cited national interests for his decision to sign a waiver on sanctions Congress voted to place on Russia.

entries.title: Brazil: Amazon deforestation lowest in nearly 40 years
entries.snippet: The latest figures show that 3,335 square kilometers of the Amazon rainforest were cleared in the year ending in July, the lowest level since 1988. The drop has been described as an "historic achievement."

entries.title: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy speaks at EU summit amid spat with Donald Trump
entries.snippet: EU leaders reaffirmed support for Ukraine at the Brussels summit. But souring relations with the US over Russia and Starlink and a big hole in the budget will make for a difficult winter for Ukraine.

entries.title: West Bank: US journalist injured by Israeli settlers
entries.snippet: Washington Post journalist Heidi Levine said she was beaten by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank. Reporters Without Borders slammed the attack as "brazen violence."

entries.title: White House press secretary Zacharia exiting role after short tenure
entries.snippet: Zacharia, having served only five days in the role, is now the shortest-serving press secretary in White House history. Her departure follows a rocky debut at the podium and controversy surrounding her background.

entries.title: Hijab ban at schools in Azerbaijan: What's behind the rare wave of protests?
entries.snippet: Girls wearing headscarves have been turned away from schools in Azerbaijan, triggering unusual protests involving children. The government rules do not mention hijabs. Why are schools enforcing unwritten rules?

entries.title: At summit, EU leaders pledge support for Ukraine's Zelenskyy
entries.snippet: President Zelenskyy has received words of encouragement from EU leaders, who pledged support for Ukraine's self-defense against Russia. This comes as winter approaches and the US seems to be withdrawing support.

entries.title: Ethiopia's Abiy Ahmed appoints interim Tigray government
entries.snippet: Abiy Ahmed's office said there would be elections held in Tigray within 6 months. The move comes after an escalation in fighting between federal forces and a rebel alliance.

entries.title: Germany, France agree on deal to support Europe's struggling car industry
entries.snippet: The two countries said the agreement aimed to safeguard Europe's automotive industry, encouraging development and research. Automakers in Europe have so far struggled to compete with Chinese electric car companies.

entries.title: Pope Leo recovering from surgery, will deliver Sunday prayer
entries.snippet: The Vatican has said that Pope Leo XIV is recovering from lung surgery. Photos released on Friday showed the pontiff celebrating Mass at Rome's Gemelli Hospital unaided.

entries.title: German colonialism on agenda in Bundestag debate on Namibia genocide
entries.snippet: Opposition parties have forced a debate in the Bundestag on the early-20th-century genocide Germany carried out in Namibia. Will this finally spur progress in addressing colonial crimes?

entries.title: Femicide in Iran: When 'honor' becomes a death sentence
entries.snippet: The murder of a young mother has once again sparked debate in Iran over so-called honor killings, the social acceptance of violence against women and the lack of protection for people vulnerable to gender-based violence.

entries.title: Albania: Students demand political change and resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama
entries.snippet: Empty lecture halls, burning buildings and demands for change: Albanian students are spearheading a protest movement that has become the biggest challenge to Prime Minister Edi Rama in years.
